speaker: donanderson
text: Great. So that's your part, right? Exactly. I thought I'd hired a newsreader for this. So for the August business showcase, rather than feature one business in Lakewood, the City Council decided to feature several businesses that have manufactured or produced products that were used to help increase safety for individuals and business during the COVID-19 pandemic. Today we want to recognize the following businesses. Custom Edge Inc., Richards Packaging Inc., and Mastro Giannis Distillery. As COVID-19 continues, we ask that if anyone knows of other Lakewood businesses that helped create safety products during the pandemic, to reach out to the business development manager at Lakewood, Becky Newton, that's b-n-e-w-t-o-n at cityoflakewood.us for further recognition. To read the full article on these businesses, go to the City's website and search business showcase. First, I'd like to talk a little bit about Custom Edge Inc. Scott and Claudine Falk started Custom Edge Inc. in 2005 in a shop off South Tacoma Way. For the past 15 years, Custom Edge has been producing custom plastic display products that are used in a variety of businesses, including retail, hospitality, and education. Products include store fixtures, museum display cases, sign and literature holders, and Lombardi trophy displays. Custom Edge has done work for many local companies as well as companies throughout the United States, Canada, and beyond. Past clients include Nordstrom, Amazon, Costco, Boeing, Microsoft, Pierce Transit, the Museum of Glass, and many more. In 2012, Custom Edge moved from Tacoma to Lakewood. The new shop, located in a part of the former Northrop Grumman facility, doubled their fabrication footprint to over 11,000 square feet, proving Custom Edge Inc., providing Custom Edge Inc. with space they needed for their growing business. When fully staffed, Custom Edge Inc. has 11 employees. When COVID-19 started, the Custom Edge Inc. team identified a new product demand, plastic safety barriers. Custom Edge started creating custom plastic barriers and shields for businesses using the same plastic materials they use for other custom fabrications. Current barrier products include freestanding barriers and table dividers. Custom Edge also created an aerosol intubation box for Swedish Hospital. Intubation boxes are used by health care workers to prevent the dispersal of infected particles during laryngectomy intubation of COVID-19 patients. So we really are proud to have Custom Edge in our community, and now I'd like to tell you a little bit about Richards Packaging. Richards Packaging was formed in Canada in 1912 as a manufacturer and distributor of glass containers for the retail drug trade and pharmaceutical industries. Today the company has locations throughout the United States and Canada and produces custom glass and plastic containers that are shipped worldwide. Since 1997, Richards Packaging has had a plastic manufacturing facility in Lakewood, located in Lakewood Industrial Business Park. When COVID-19 pandemic started, Richards Packaging was called on to help produce containers to keep up with the world's unprecedented demand for sanitizing solutions. Richards dusted off a mold last used in 2005 to make one-gallon containers that Great Pacific Packaging in Fife filled with commercial-grade disinfectant. Richards Packaging Inc. has also modified an existing pill bottle that an Oregon customer purchased to fill with hand sanitizer. Now in the third recognition tonight, I'd like to talk about Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery. Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery is no stranger to the Lakewood Business Showcase, having been featured as the Business Showcase in March of 2019. Six months ago, at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, hand sanitizer was identified as a way to help reduce the spread of the virus, particularly when hand washing was not possible. In March and April, hand sanitizer and toilet paper became the hottest commodities, leading to shortages across the nation, including in the Puget Sound region. Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery knew they could help meet the local need for hand sanitizer. After receiving the green light from the FDA, Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery started producing hand sanitizer. Rather than sell the product, the distillery decided to donate it to organizations at the forefront of the COVID-19 response. First responders, hospitals, and government agencies. Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery donated hand sanitizer to Swedish Hospital, the Auburn Police Department, private ambulance companies, Westpierce Fire and Rescue, and the City of Lakewood. In total, they donated over 50 gallons of hand sanitizer during the shortage. While currently, Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery is no longer producing hand sanitizer, now that industry is caught up to meet the demand, the hand sanitizer it did produce in March and April helped fill the significant void in the greater Puget Sound community. It is because of these companies' responses to the COVID-19 pandemic that Lakewood City Council recognizes Custom Edge Inc., Richards Packaging Inc., and Mastro Giannis Distillery and Winery as its August 2020 business showcases. So we really appreciate you folks, hopefully somebody's out there listening to us and we'll get you some physical representation of our recognition in a short order, but thanks again for all you do and thanks for being part of the business community in the City of Lakewood. We now move to the next item of business, the Port of Tacoma strategic plan update, and for this we have an old friend, a retired judge and present Port

speaker: johnmccarthy
text: Commissioner John McCarthy. Good evening Mayor Anderson, can you hear me now? Yes. All right, thank you Mayor, Council members, City Manager Caulfield. My name is John McCarthy and I'm the Port of Tacoma Commission President this year. On behalf of my fellow commissioners, I want to thank you for the opportunity to share with you and the citizens of Lakewood information about the Port of Tacoma strategic planning process and the many ways that input and feedback can be directed to the Port. With screen sharing it's often difficult to see if someone has a question, so if you don't mind I'm prepared to make my presentation and then answer any questions at the end of the presentation. Sounds like a good idea. Okay, thank you. To start, some background on the Port might help set context and explain the importance of our strategic planning process. Washington is the most trade dependent state in the nation with 40 percent of its jobs related to international trade. The Port of Tacoma is considered one of the region's economic engines and as half of the Northwest Seaport Alliance along with Seattle, we are the fourth largest container gateway region in the United States. A study released in 2019 highlighted the economic impacts of the Port's real estate and marine cargo operations in 2017. At that time the study showed that the Port supported more than 41, excuse me, 42,000 jobs. It generated nearly three billion dollars in economic activity. It produced more than 100 million dollars annually in state and local taxes to support education, police, fire services, and road improvements as well as some other things. In addition, the Port partners with many Pierce County jurisdictions on infrastructure projects that support economic development and tourism activities. The Port most recently participated and partnered with Lakewood on the signalization at the intersection of Durango and Steilacoom Boulevard as well as road construction in the Spring Brook area and at 146th Street Southwest. Lakewood recognizes that a healthy community relies on a combination of residential, commercial, and industrial lands. A diverse portfolio of business opportunities in your community means that your citizens do not have to sit in traffic as they drive to another community to work. A diverse economy was one of the main reasons that the Port initially purchased land for an industrial and manufacturing area in the Fredrickson area in 1968. What was once bare land without utilities is now a successful manufacturing and industrial center for companies like Boeing and IKEA and more importantly an area offering thousands of family wage jobs. The military is also an important economic contributor not only to the health of Lakewood but also the Port of Tacoma and our nation. The Port is a Department of Defense designated strategic port under the National Port Readiness Network. We are positioned to support force deployment during contingencies and other national defense emergencies. Throughout the course of the year the Port will handle multiple missions in support of JBLM as the military moves hardware to and from locations around the globe. There is a heavy outbound armored vehicle dispatch scheduled to take place at the end of September and also the 883rd Transportation Battalion is planning another large outloading before the end of the year. Our previous strategic plan was prepared prior to the formation of the Northwest Seaport Alliance which occurred five years ago. When the commission hired its new executive director Eric Johnson about a year ago one of the first directions was for him to begin working on a strategic plan that focused on the non-marine cargo businesses in which the Port can statutorily engage. That is where we need your good ideas your input and your feedback and the feedback from the citizens that you represent. As if you can't already tell I'm really excited about this work and excited about hearing from you and your citizens and as well as all of our constituents and this is where you can come in because you know your constituents we need to hear your ideas and feedback to identify the next big economic development opportunities that are important to Lakewood's citizens. So if you could show our first slide it's a timeline of our schedule for the strategic plan. The firm of Mahl, Foster and Elangi is the consulting firm that's helping us on this project and they've prepared this timeline for a high level overview of our strategic plan process. Public engagement is essential to the success of this planning process and we'll be reaching out to ask for feedback at key milestones along the way. Although the process is expected to go into the first quarter of 2021 it is important to provide feedback early so they can be incorporated into the commission's discussions on goals and initiatives. So how can you provide input if you would please turn to the next slide. First is to visit our online open house at www.portoflacoma.com open house. I think one of our most effective outreach tools especially in our current COVID environment is our online strategic plan open house website. This will remain open for a few months and I encourage you to perhaps talk to your constituents and yourself if you would to spend some time on this site to find more out about the strategic plan process and our draft goal ideas which at this point include economic development, infrastructure, real estate, the environment and more. The next slide please. Take our online survey and while you're there please provide your ideas and input by taking the survey. Again the link for this website is www.openhouse.portoflacoma.com. Finally the next slide give us a call. Call this number. We'll get feedback from you. Many of you I know and all of the members of our commissioner would like to hear personally from you as to what you hear from your constituents or give us a call and we don't want to miss any ideas. So even the old-fashioned phone calls to connect with people is a key ingredient of our strategic planning process. The next slide please. Finally send us an email at strategicplanatportoftacoma.com. So here's what I would ask you to consider doing to assist in this process. Please talk to your constituents. Share your thoughts on current partnerships that the port may have with municipalities, the county and other organizations. Talk about potential processes and opportunities in freight infrastructure projects but we also want to hear new ideas. Is there another Fredrickson out there somewhere in Pierce County that can generate jobs or how can we better support Lakewood's economic development initiatives? Please take the time to make sure that your voice is heard during this process to develop this new strategic plan for Pierce County's port. Thank you for the time today and I'm happy to answer any questions that you might have for me. Thank you very much.

speaker: davebugher
text: members of the council and the mayor. This evening's consideration is a proposed resolution that would certify Lakewood as quote unquote a coordinated community applicant under Pierce County's temporary shelter program grant application. The application lets Lakewood join with three other cities in Pierce County to increase temporary shelter funding for Pierce County region wide. If Lakewood, Puyallup, Tacoma and UP sign on as coordinated community applicants the county receives 4.7 million versus 3.8 million dollars in grant funds. I would describe this as Lakewood acting something like a pass-through agency. Pierce County remains the applicant and fiduciary agent. As long as the city remains a coordinated community applicant there is no fiscal impact upon the city. The recommendation this evening is to approve the resolution which in essence provides more money to Pierce County to increase temporary shelter bed capacity in Tacoma and somewhere in East Pierce County the site of which is to be yet determined. I'd like to provide some quick background information on this. Department of Commerce has proposed this new grant in what is described as temporary shelters. Funds are coming from the state's general fund to increase again local temporary shelter capacity in Snohomish, King and Pierce County. Department of Commerce is requiring a quick turnaround time for approvals but has not been a very smooth process. Their application has been modified three times. Pierce County's application deadline has been extended twice and the county we found out today does not wish to extend a third time. Current application deadline is Friday August 21st but the county is trying to get its application submitted by this Thursday August 20th. The application is again for two temporary shelters. One for movable tiny homes in Tacoma and another at an unspecified Lakewood unspecified location in East Pierce County sponsored by Puyallup. We found out late last week that the county may be under budget by about a million dollars and so there was some investigation as to who might be able to use these additional funds. Lakewood began to explore this. We had a follow-up meeting this afternoon. There are some questions we asked and we finally received some answers. Will Pierce County extend the application a period a third time? Again the answer is no. What does Lakewood have to do if we wish to participate? The answer is to become a lead grantee applicant, sign confirmation of same and commit to a specific number of temporary shelter beds by 5 p.m August 20th and have those beds available by December 1st. Is Pierce County really under budget by one million dollars? Not really. Tacoma is going to need more fund more money for its program. There's also another project in the background an expansion of Tacoma's women's rescue mission. Most of the million dollars is going to be spent. If Lakewood did have access to the grant could Lakewood use the grant money to buy beds for either the Salvation Army or the Tacoma rescue mission? Again the answer was no. The grant requires that we create new beds and again if Lakewood did have access to the grant could the grant cover some of the city's admin costs? The answer is yes but we really don't know what that looks like. So the end result was everybody agreed that Lakewood was not ready but I appreciate the fact that we made an effort. speaker: johncaulfield
text: Thank you Mayor Anderson. Good evening Deputy Mayor, council members. A few updates for you. So on the federal front it's not so good news. So I think as you're all aware the congress has been having some discussions about a fourth economic stimulus package that hopefully would include financial relief for local governments. The negotiations did break down the negotiations were with the house and with the white house the administration directly. The senate was not involved in the negotiations in any shape form or manner and the reason being is because the senate as a whole couldn't come to a decision or an understanding of what they would or could could support. The house as you know did pass the heroes act a three trillion dollar proposal a number of months ago which would have which includes 350 billion dollars for local and state and state government. The white house proposed a one trillion dollar stimulus package however that stimulus package did not include assistance financial assistance for local and state government. However the house did propose a middle of the ground a two trillion dollar package and invited the white house and the administration to negotiate on that in terms of what could be supported. However again those discussions went nowhere and the congress has adjourned for their summer recess and are not expected to get together again until the early the early part of of september. The one bit of message that we continue to get from our delegation in Washington state is that ultimately they there will be a deal but again I think as you're all aware we have been hearing this for a good number of months. Hopefully here in the near future congress will will do something. In the meantime we are going to move forward with preparing a 20 to 21 22 proposed budget and that's the that's the best that we can do with the information with the information that that that we have. On to DSEP the defense community infrastructure program. I think as reported last week unfortunately our project was not selected. We did go back and review the projects that were selected and basically it was 13 projects. For the most part they were community centers, recreation centers, swimming pools, things along those lines. You know obviously we're very very disappointed that the city of Lakewood was not was not chosen. I can also tell you that our key sponsor congressman Heck was not happy. Likewise representative Kilmer and representative Smith who is the chair of the house armed services committee are also not pleased that not only was Lakewood not chosen but any project that was submitted in Washington state was not selected particularly given our footprint as it relates to the military. We are going to continue to move forward with a legislative fix. A matter of fact both Mr. Kilmer and Mr. Heck have been using language prepared by the city of Lakewood which focuses on two areas. One is to put the infrastructure back in the DCIP which is these monies need to be used for road, street, transportation, utility improvements and then secondly that the match go back to what was originally proposed which is 30 percent from the current 50 percent. That language has been has been proposed as part of the NDAA which is the authorization component of the annual defense bill. In addition it's also been proposed in the appropriations bill for the defense budget so we have it moving forward on both fronts and it does have strong support in the house so we'll certainly keep you appraised of that. The other areas in the area of transportation I think as you'll recall our representative Mr. Heck and others has been working with congressman Larson from up north regarding the build up which formerly was the tiger program to having a set aside for medium-sized cities. This is something that the city of Lakewood has been involved with now going on about five years. There's 17 cities in Washington state medium-sized cities that are supportive of this however the amendment that was offered by Mr. Larson that would have accommodated this was ruled out of order on the house side at both the authorization and the appropriations level so it's not moving forward this session so we will regroup continue to work with our partner cities here in Washington state and try and figure out how do we move forward. Just a reminder that actually five years ago the house actually passed this and then it got held up in the senate so now we're back to kind of square one and trying to get it to the house but again that's the update in terms of what's happening or rather not what's happening in the other Washington and Washington in Washington DC. On the economic development front last week you may have seen an article that Amazon released regarding their Seattle footprint asking their employees where they wanted to work and where they wanted to live. Overwhelmingly apparently the Amazon employees denoted anywhere except for Seattle they pointed out areas such as the east side over in the Bellevue Redmond area but also down south in Auburn and Tacoma and Pierce County. As soon as I saw that article I called the first thing in the morning I called our good friend Bruce Kendall over at the Tacoma Pierce County Economic Development Board and the reason being is because we don't have a direct line to Amazon however the EDB does given our work regarding the H2 headquarters work that we were all involved in with the EDB and the leadership role. The EDB was appreciative of the information that we provided. You know I pointed out not just Pierce County but specifically Lakewood would certainly be well suited to entertain having Amazon come to our community. There's a couple of reasons for that. Number one is because there are some definite locations right now one being Lakewood Landing out on Pacific Highway South and then the other right here in our town center would be a prime location for them for them as well but then secondly you know the cost of doing business here in Lakewood from a regulatory standpoint is not it's one of the lowest if not the lowest around including not having a B&O tax. So we'll continue to have conversations with the EDB and hopefully we'll be in conversation with Amazon here as a region in the near future. Likewise the EDB has been having conversations and been reaching out to REI as well who have recognized that they no longer need a major headquarters over on the east side and they're looking to spread out their footprint so that their employees can have different locations of where to not just work but also live and again the Tacoma Pierce County Lakewood area is an area that those employees have an interest in. I'm also pleased to announce that our Friendship City, the City of Gimhae, the Republic of South Korea so so gracious. They sent last week we received 10,000 face masks and they're N-94s and this is what they this is what they look like. They're actually very good to use you get a little bit of space between your mouth and the mask and in addition earlier today we received a thousand sets of personal protective equipment and as it relates to the masks we're going to look at how we can make those available to our to our community and maybe set something up here in City Hall and allow people to drive through and and grab a mask or two or however many they need from their family. We're also working on a news release to get this out in the media. Again this is a big big deal for again our Friendship City, Gimhae to to do this for us and just a very wonderful gesture on on their part so look for a news release and some pictures on this in the next in the in the next day or so. Also along the lines of COVID-19 our team here at the City as you as you're aware has been having conversations with Pierce County DEM Department of Emergency Management as well as our local health district and we have been able to secure three upcoming opportunities for people in Lakewood to go and get tested for the COVID or free test. The first one will actually be tomorrow Tuesday August 18th over in the Springbrook neighborhood at Springbrook Park from 10 to 3 followed by Friday August 28th over on Lakewood Drive at the Lakewood Community Center the where our Senior Activity Center is and then lastly over at Fort Steilacoom Park on Thursday September 3rd again from 10 to 3. This is part of the mobile testing site that the Pierce County DEM has and they expect to be able to test you know three to five hundred people during that five hour five hour time so if you haven't gotten tested now's the time to go do it and again we are getting the news out to our to our neighborhood. If you do decide to show up I do suggest that you get there early maybe at 9 30 or so to get in the queue usually takes about an hour an hour and a half to kind of work through you know the line if you will. The you know every year our police department is eligible to receive a justice assistance grant which is funds that are allocated by Congress that then flow down through through the state and then come to local jurisdictions such as Lakewood. As a part of that process we're required to brief the City Council in an open public meeting and then there's an opportunity for public feedback for a month. We do have a deadline of having all that completed by October 1st so as part of your next study session which is a week from today on August 24th we will be presenting Council with the components of that grant. Really we're looking to use the funds which total about forty thousand dollars in two areas. The first is to is to replace a good number of our bicycles for our bike patrol. Many of them are you know 10 to 15 years old and then secondly to replace a repeater for cellular and internet services over at our over at our police station. There's a project in our stormwater capital improvement program that's actually been there for a good number of years. It's to do some retrofitting as it relates to water quality over in the Oak Brook neighborhood. Our public works engineering director Paul Busich asked his staff to do a bit of a more deep dive into that and long story short that evaluation showed that this neighborhood does not have a water quality or flow issue so there's no need to do those do those improvements. So we'll be returning the balance of those dollars to the stormwater CIP which will become available for reappropriation as part of your upcoming biannual budget. That will be less the monies that we use to go through the evaluation which was about $32,000 or so. You might recall two years ago the humane society had some changes in regards to the amount of money that they're charging for animal shelter services and that was pretty significant. We have looked at a couple of other options for animal shelter but really at this point in time there aren't any and so we have gone back to the table and talked to the humane society about continuing with them because again there's really nobody else in the county that we could do this for and so we're looking to enter into a four-year agreement that would result in a four percent increase in 21, seven and a half percent in 22, eight and a half percent in 23 and kind of a cola plus one percent in 2024 to lock us down over a four-year biennium. The purpose of the increases is that the humane society going back a number of years you know over a decade a decade and a half they did not keep up with charging their users such as cities you know the appropriate cost and so that contract is expected to come forward to you for review and consideration here in the next month or two. On the transportation side I wanted to let you know that our public works engineering department and submitted for the maximum number of transportation improvement board or TIB grant projects. The first one was 100th Avenue between Lakeview and South Tacoma Way. That's a three and a half million dollar project and so we requested 80 percent or 2.8 million dollars. The second project is Custer Road the part of Custer that needs some work from a little bit due east of Bridgeport to 75th Street which would include full curbs gutters and sidewalks. That project cost for that segment is three million dollars and again we're requesting 80 percent or 2.4 million dollars. And then the third project is Gravely Lake Drive which is a component of the JPLM North Access Project which we are going to move forward with in 2021 since it's all designed and it is fully funded and that's a seven and a half million dollar project and we're going to ask TIB for three million dollars and then in turn that would free up three million dollars that we could allocate elsewhere in support of the JBLM North Access Project to complete that. Out of the three projects we actually believe that the Gravely Lake Project probably has the best chance out of all three for a number of reasons. One is it connects in with the Interstate 5 and Pacific Highway South. It also connects in with Veterans Drive and then lastly it's the last final segment of Gravely Lake Drive between again Interstate 5 all the way to Stillicum Boulevard. We will know more on those grant applications in terms of whether or not we'll have been awarded funding when the TIB board meets in the latter part of November. Another grant that we took a look at was the State Public Works Board put out a call for a broadband grant and loan program. We took a very close and detailed look at that and had some conversations with folks at the state. Long story short you know there's really what they told us is this grant is really geared toward more of the rural areas. As a matter of fact a number of the planning grants there was nine of them that they awarded about a year ago are all out in kind of rural areas and were awarded to PUDs and Economic Development Boards. However we did take a look at it but also you know the speed of our internet and broadband service here in Lakewood is much much greater than what we would have to have to even qualify to apply for the grant but I just wanted to let the Mayor and Council know that we did take a look at that. Earlier this spring you know we notified you that our publishing company that helps with Lakewood Connections magazine unfortunately is going out of business. We did go through an RFQ process to select a new vendor and we got some good bids. Actually the lowest and most responsible bidder is a firm called Journal Graphics who actually was a sub for Phillips Publishing so they're somewhat familiar with Lakewood. In addition they'll be able to continue to do the three magazines that we do a year also with their cost with some graphic design and then of course you know the mailing costs. The costs are actually just a tiny little bit lower than what they were with Phillips Publishing and actually would include 16 pages which is similar to what the other magazine what our regular magazine was when you take out all the advertising and things along those lines. So the number and size of of the magazine will be the same as as our citizens get today. And then lastly you know knock on wood hopefully we'll be able to move forward at this point in time we plan on doing it. So if you haven't seen Sandlot great kids movie about about baseball and a big old dog. So with that Mayor that's my report.
